candidates.name: Malignant Melanoma
support_spans: Initial histopathologic findings showed a Breslow thickness of 6 mm, 14 mitotic figures/mm2
Frontal nerve biopsy: Cross section of nerve showing malignant cells with mitotic activity
candidates.why: The patient's history of a recurring forehead lesion with initial histopathologic findings consistent with melanoma and subsequent biopsy showing malignant cells supports this diagnosis.

candidates.name: Perineural Invasion by Malignant Melanoma
support_spans: extensive perineural and intraneural invasion
MRI finding: Left superior orbit mass extending along the supraorbital nerve to the cavernous sinus
candidates.why: The patient's history of perineural invasion and the MRI findings of a mass extending along the supraorbital nerve support this diagnosis.

candidates.name: Orbital Metastasis of Malignant Melanoma
support_spans: Left proptosis and resistance to globe retropulsion with edema, erythema, and ptosis of the left upper eyelid
MRI finding: Left superior orbit mass extending along the supraorbital nerve to the cavernous sinus
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and MRI findings are consistent with an orbital metastasis of malignant melanoma.

candidates.name: Neurotropic melanoma
support_spans: extensive perineural and intraneural invasion
Intense enhancement of the V1 branch of the left frontal nerve with associated fat stranding
candidates.why: The patient's presentation of nerve involvement, including forehead anesthesia in the V1 division of the trigeminal nerve and imaging findings of intense enhancement of the V1 branch of the left frontal nerve, suggests neurotropic melanoma.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may deserve minority protection because it is a rare and aggressive subtype of melanoma that can be easily missed if not considered in the differential diagnosis.

candidates.why: The patient's presentation of diplopia, proptosis, and limited adduction on the left, along with imaging findings of a left superior orbit mass extending to the cavernous sinus, suggests cavernous sinus syndrome.
